data.title: feat(ostool): 支持可选 ELF 调试产物与元数据解析
data.body:
新增可选的反汇编、ELF 信息和符号列表产物，支持 Cargo 和自定义构建，默认关闭。

在 `.build.toml` 中启用：

```toml
[artifacts.analysis]
disassembly = true
elf_info = true
symbols = true
```

- 产物写在原始 ELF 旁，文件名分别追加 `.disassembly`、`.elf-info`、`.symbols`。
- ELF 信息包含架构、入口地址、加载段和可用的 `__executable_start`；缺失该符号不会导致构建失败。
- 分析读取原始 ELF，避免运行时副本剥离符号的影响。
- 每次构建重新生成已启用的产物；工具缺失、ELF 无效或生成失败时明确报错。

data.title: stm32/flash: preserve PSIZE during programming cleanup
data.body: Programming cleanup on STM32F2/F4/F7 and H7 resets PSIZE from x32 to x8, causing subsequent erases to use x8. Use modify instead of write during cleanup to preserve PSIZE while clearing PG and the applicable interrupt enables.

data.title: stm32/flash: preserve PSIZE during programming cleanup
data.body:
Programming on STM32F2/F4/F7 and H7 selects x32 parallelism, but the cleanup writes a zero-initialized control register and resets PSIZE to x8. The next erase inherits x8. This PR preserves the existing x32 setting when programming finishes.

- Scope

    Change the six programming cleanup writes from `write` to `modify`, retaining PSIZE while clearing PG and the existing async interrupt enables. Programming setup and bank/region routing remain unchanged. H7A/B has no PSIZE field; its existing conditional compilation and control-bit cleanup remain intact.

- Validation

    On an **STM32H723VGT6**, the same RAM-resident test program was built against baseline `96be1098` and this patch. The blocking path completed two erase → program → readback cycles in each build:

    - Baseline: PSIZE was x8 after both writes and the second erase.
    - Patched: PSIZE remained x32 after both writes and the second erase; PG was cleared and Flash was locked.
    - Both builds returned the expected data. Checking PSIZE directly distinguished the regression from successful readback alone.

    Software checks passed: 11 ARM library configurations covering F207, F407, F429, F732, F769, H723, H743, H7A3 and H7B3, including applicable single/dual-bank configurations; six existing host-test configurations; all five existing F4/F7/H7 Flash examples; formatting and diff checks.

    Hardware coverage of the patch is limited to H723 blocking operations. Patched async/region paths and other chips were not tested on hardware. Attempting to program FF over zeroes did not produce a hardware error, so hardware-error return paths remain unverified. Host tests and builds do not establish register behavior.

- Compatibility

    No configuration API or programming parallelism default changes. This preserves the x32 selected at programming entry; it does not restore an arbitrary earlier PSIZE or guarantee x32 for the first erase. F4's cancel-time `OnDrop` also uses the updated cleanup, but no cancellation wait/recovery logic or safety guarantee is added. The existing H7 cancellation limitation remains.

- Notes

    No example changes are included. Configurable erase parallelism in embassy-rs/embassy#7044 is a separate concern. Codex was used as an aid during implementation and validation.

data.title: stm32/flash: add optional erase parallelism
data.body:
While using the STM32H723VGT6, I found that Flash erase speed was slow. After reading the driver code, I confirmed that there is currently no configurable erase parallelism option, so I am submitting this PR to allow applications to select the erase parallelism based on the chip and power supply conditions.

```rust
let mut config = Config::default();
config.erase_parallelism = Some(EraseParallelism::X32);
let flash = Flash::new_blocking_with_config(p.FLASH, config);
```

- Scope

    This PR provides **X8, X16, X32, and X64** configurations for:

    - STM32F2/F4/F7
    - H7 series with PSIZE

    It covers blocking, async, and split region paths. H7A/B does not have PSIZE and is **not** supported in this PR.

- Validation

    Hardware validation has been completed on the **STM32H723VGT6**, covering:

    - All four configurations
    - Default behavior
    - Region path
    - Erase, write-readback, and re-erase

- Compatibility

    The original constructor remains compatible. The default `None` preserves the current PSIZE without actively modifying it; once the user specifies a parallelism, the driver applies that configuration before each erase, including the next erase after a write operation changes PSIZE.

    Callers must meet the corresponding power supply and VPP requirements for the chip.

- Discussion

    One point worth discussing: should `None` be removed and callers be required to explicitly select the erase parallelism? It is currently kept for compatibility with existing behavior.

- Notes

    Codex was used as an aid during implementation and validation.

data.title: stm32/flash: add optional erase parallelism
data.body:
STM32F2/F4/F7 and `flash_h7` erase routines inherit PSIZE from the register state, which programming can change. This adds an optional erase-parallelism selection through `flash::Config` and the `new_with_config` / `new_blocking_with_config` constructors.

```rust
let mut config = Config::default();
config.erase_parallelism = Some(EraseParallelism::X32);
let flash = Flash::new_blocking_with_config(p.FLASH, config);
```

Existing constructors remain source-compatible and use `None`, which leaves PSIZE unchanged, including changes made by writes. An explicit selection is applied before each sector erase and retained by both region-splitting methods. Programming access width, erase units, address layout, and existing error handling are unchanged.

Callers must satisfy the selected device's voltage/VPP requirements throughout the erase. F2/F4/F7 x64 requires external VPP where supported; H7 has different electrical limits. The driver does not measure supply voltage. STM32H7A/B is excluded because its FLASH peripheral has no PSIZE selection; see the [ST register definitions](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/cmsis-device-h7/blob/master/Include/stm32h7a3xx.h).

Validation in a Linux development container:

- All five STM32 host-test configurations from `.github/ci/test.sh` passed: F429VG single/dual bank, F732ZE, and F769NI single/dual bank.
- ARM library builds with `-Dwarnings` passed for F207ZG, F429VG, F732ZE, H723ZG, H7A3ZI, H7B3AI, G474RE, and F103C8, covering supported and unaffected conditional branches.
- Changed Rust files passed the repository's nightly formatter; `git diff --check` passed.

Hardware validation at `4bfdd3e0761c85b4aea60d3655600ecab552cf45`:

- Tested an STM32H723VGT6 (single-bank, 1 MiB Flash) on an EHA Controller. The schematic specifies a 3.3 V MCU supply; supply voltage was not measured during this run.
- A temporary RAM-resident program called this branch's public Flash APIs on one initially erased 128 KiB sector. All 12 cases passed: X8/X16/X32/X64 in blocking and async modes, both original constructors with the default `None`, and blocking/async region splitting.
- Explicit selections were checked against a different preset PSIZE. Each case erased, wrote/read back one 32-byte Flash word, then erased again and checked the entire sector for `0xFF`. Register checks confirmed that explicit settings were reapplied after writes and that `None` preserved the current PSIZE.
- A full 1 MiB Flash dump was byte-identical before and after the test, and the original application was restarted.

The async cases used a polling runner, so they do not independently verify executor wakeups. Other MCU families, dual-bank hardware, cancellation/power-loss behavior, and electrical/timing limits were not tested on hardware.

The PR retains the existing tests and does not add a host register-emulation harness or the temporary hardware-test program.
